text.p: Israel's Bank Hapoalim values Blue Square Chain Stores Properties & Investments at $267 million to $280 million against a market value of $214 million on September 3, the bank said in a report on Tuesday.

The report estimates the company's earnings per share will rise to 2.01 shekels in 1996 and 2.19 shekels in 1997 against 1.68 in 1995. The share price is estimated to rise to 27-29 shekels in the coming 12 months against 23.12 currently, the bank said.
The company owns a network of supermarkets and department stores.

Sales of the company are expected to reach 2.423 billion shekels in 1996 and 2.810 billion in 1997 against 1.922 billion in 1995. The report said the company is increasing sales steadily mainly by opening centres on new sites and entering new marketing niches.
The company is a subsidiary of Blue Square Israel, which raised $66 million in a share offering in New York in July.
The report said it believes the New York offering will allow the company to further develop and to lower its credit dependence on banks and other credit agencies.

At the same time growing competition in the local market has lowered profit margins and induced the company to undertake aggressive advertising and high marketing costs. An estimated slowdown in private consumption and Israel's gross domestic product in the coming year will also hurt the rate of growth of the stores, the report said.
